body.heading: Four Asks, Five Arms, Ten Files Ported Verbatim
body.html: Stem Shovel shipped the Study 12 alignment and the Study 13 reconciler within hours of each report and sent back four validation asks. Study 14 runs all of them on verbatim ports pinned at the app's own commits: the alignment set, the reconciler utilities, and the band-markdown parsers. Five arms, about $0.40 of a $2 fence (two model calls in the reconciler arm), one registered amendment.

body.heading: What Validates Exactly
body.html: G1 passed exactly: the app's parsers round-trip the bench's material bar for bar and section for section (76 of 76 and 86 of 86 on the two transcriptions, 24 of 24 on a marked measure summary, and the 6/8-in-eighths convention rendering the app's bar seconds to the millisecond), which means future bench studies can feed production's own parsers instead of maintaining ports. G3's aligner clause held too: fed through its own parser path, the shipped aligner reproduces Study 12's precision, six of eight non-edge boundaries within 0.11 seconds of the band's declared starts, aligning a 141-second song in 1.1 seconds.

body.heading: The Constant Caught Before Release
body.html: G2 is the study's reason to exist. The shipped same-piece constant, a tritone-probe ratio threshold of 3, was set from synthetic numbers where right charts score 24 to 49. On the real recordings, right charts score 2.04 and 2.53, both below 3, so samePiece returns false on the band's own correct charts, every placement gets hedged, and the song-check card would tell the band their chart does not seem to match their own recording. Amendment 1 measured what the registered pairs could not see, the real-domain wrong charts: 1.17 and 1.24. On real audio the control separates cleanly, wrongs at or below 1.24 and rights at or above 2.04, just not at 3. The recommendation went back at about 1.6, the real-domain midpoint, with the caveats owned in the report: two pairs per class, one band, and a 1.6-times margin where Study 12 had an order of magnitude. The home-field lesson's third appearance, and this time caught before a release instead of after one. Study 15 has since run the shipped constant at three right charts and six wrong pairs: it survives, by two hundredths, and the local-cost clause flagged here as the second check is what restores the margin.

body.heading: The Reconciler Needs Nothing, and the Edges Are Measured
body.html: G4 passed with a bonus: under production's shipped thinking configuration, the reconciler scores 44 of 76 with 15 fixes and zero breaks, beating the bench's thinking-off measurement of 41 in half the output tokens, because adaptive thinking absorbs the per-bar narration that forced Study 13's cap amendment. Zero breaks now stand across every reconciler run in two studies, and the verdict on the reconciler is: leave it as shipped. Arm D measured the two edge rules the app asked about: the first-onset snap repairs both real intros outright (7.15 and 2.41 seconds to 0.00), and the last-sound rule repairs the 9.11-second outro miss to 0.03 seconds while inheriting chart quality exactly as feared (it would worsen the song whose outro length the bench's transcription guessed wrong), so both ship gated on samePiece and hedged.

body.heading: The Loop, Four Times Around in 36 Hours
body.html: The scorecard: 1 right; 2 wrong in the direction that matters, since the real-domain collapse of the ratio was unpredicted and the amendment exists precisely because the registered pairs could not see it; 3 half; 4 right; 5 half. And the thread note this page exists to carry: request, ship, validate, catch, fix shipped, four times around the loop in under 36 hours. Stem Shovel has already taken the recommendation, the constant now sits at 1.6 in production, and their engineering log carries the standing rule the catch earned: a constant gating real recordings is provisional until measured on real recordings.

body.heading: The Constant Survives by Two Hundredths
body.html: G1 passed, barely. The three right-chart ratios land at 2.04, 3.21 and 2.53, and all six wrong cross-pairs stay below 1.6, but the two new pairings involving Peaceful Dreams land at 1.57 and 1.58, a margin of two hundredths. The constant survives its first expansion of n and is officially thin: same-key, same-tonality wrong pairings close most of the gap the Study 14 pairs showed.

body.heading: The Deliverable: the Second Clause, Stated by Number
body.html: G3 passed clean, and it is the study's deliverable: the second same-piece clause the app asked for, stated by number exactly as the 1.6 was derived. The real-domain median per-bar local costs separate completely, right charts at 0.172 to 0.243 against wrong charts at 0.365 to 0.482, so the recommended clause is median local cost at or below 0.30, AND-ed with the ratio. The complementarity is the headline: the ratio's two 0.02-margin near-misses carry medians of 0.365 and 0.400, comfortably caught, so the two clauses fail in different directions and together restore the margin the ratio lost. Disclosed per the home-field rule: three synthetic wrong pairs would pass both clauses, in a domain production never sees.

body.heading: The Gate That Failed by Its Own Letter
body.html: G2 failed, and the anatomy splits three ways. First, the edge rules work where they were aimed: letter-lands' intro miss of 3.61 seconds goes to 0.00 and its outro miss of 9.11 to 0.08, and peaceful's intro lands at 0.00. Second, peaceful's outro lands 3.33 seconds late against the 1.0-second gate: a 20-bar single-chord decay rings out above audibleSpan's 2 percent floor, inflating the LAST-SOUND anchor, a real and bounded residual left open with the app as one more refinement. Third, the bench mis-drafted its own interior clause, writing a no-regression intent as an absolute ceiling that letter-lands' pre-existing stragglers never met in any prior study; the data shows zero interior regressions against Study 14's values, and the gate fails by the letter the bench wrote. Registration lesson seven: a no-regression clause must name its baseline, not restate a hope.

body.heading: Verdict, Scorecard, and the Queue
body.html: The scorecard: 1 right, including eat-all-the-clocks near 2.5; 2 half, with both intros and letter's outro repaired exactly as traced while peaceful's ring-out residual and the mis-drafted clause went unpredicted; 3 right in full, including the margin claim. The verdict delivered: v0.201.2's constant and edge rules are registered as validated at n of 3 right and 6 wrong with the margin stated; the local-cost clause is no longer optional belt and braces, it is what restores the same-piece check's margin; and the LAST-SOUND refinement for long ring-outs stays open. Study 16 is queued by the app's chart-idiom response: re-running on the band's five stored chart texts through the production parser once that work lands, with one point of record corrected on the way, since their Peaceful Dreams eight-bar audit predates the band's revision, whose stored text now parses 152 bars clean. Study 16 has since run on the migrated charts: all four gates pass, and a real wrong pair finally crosses the 1.6 ratio gate at 1.74, rejected only by this study's local-cost clause, which turned the recommendation from prophylactic to urgent.

body.heading: The Adoption, and the Registration
body.html: Stem Shovel retired its in-house chord-chart parser and adopted the open barmark standard end to end: barmark 0.5.0 from npm parses every chart behind a production adapter, the renderer draws from the same parse, and sections are known by name rather than numeral (the app's pins 371831ae, b5ed9ed2 and a0926c65). All five stored Badverbs charts were migrated under a refuse-not-guess rule and confirmed by the band against its recordings' section markers; the four public ones are the corpus, fetched verbatim, with the fifth not on a public page and disclosed as out of scope. Registered at b589daf with one amendment, recorded before results were accepted, for handling a refusal in the exploratory cross-pairs. Zero spend, 95 mechanically graded cells, no model calls, and the alignment ports unchanged from Study 15's pin.

body.heading: The Parsers Agree Bar for Bar
body.html: G1 passed with nothing to report, which is the point. The three committed app-dialect texts ran through the retired chordChartBars parser and through barmark 0.5.0 behind the production adapter, identical bodies with each parser reading its own registered dialect header: 76, 152 and 86 bars, zero differences under the registered per-bar comparison, zero warnings from either parser. Nothing the app could read was lost in the adoption.

body.heading: The Migration Is Grid-Perfect
body.html: G2 passed at a precision the gate did not ask for. The gate allowed each band-declared section start within a tenth of a second on the chart's own grid; every public migrated chart lands every declared start at 0.0000 seconds with zero parser warnings. letter-lands parses 76 bars with 10 sections, peaceful-dreams 153 with 10 (the verified 152 plus the grammar's ring-out attack bar), eat-all-the-clocks 71 with 9 in the band's corrected play-order form, and exploratory mop-heart 140 with 8, in 3/4 at 224 bpm with a mid-chart key change. letter-lands and peaceful-dreams also match the verified content lists exactly under the registered normalization.

body.heading: A Real Wrong Pair Finally Crosses the Ratio Gate
body.html: G3 passed, and it carries the study's headline. The right pairs pass both same-piece clauses comfortably: ratios 1.90, 3.18 and 2.63 with median local costs of 0.177 to 0.210, plus exploratory mop-heart's first-ever alignment at 1.96 and 0.248. All six registered wrong pairs fail, ratios 1.13 to 1.57, caught by local costs of 0.333 to 0.475. Then the exploratory cross-pairs delivered what three studies of eroding margin predicted: the eat-all-the-clocks recording against the mop-heart chart scores ratio 1.74, the first real wrong pair above the 1.6 gate, and is rejected only by the second clause, its median local cost of 0.323 sitting over the 0.30 line. Production's shipped samePiece is still ratio-only, so the bench's standing recommendation to AND the local-cost clause in is now urgent rather than prophylactic: a real catalog pair crosses the ratio gate. One other exploratory pair never produced a number at all, and that is also a result: production's own rule that a chart running more than twice the recording's length must be refused turned the mop-heart recording against the peaceful-dreams chart away, the right answer by construction.

body.heading: No Regression, the Chart Was the Bottleneck, and the Verdict
body.html: G4 passed against its named baseline: through the entirely new parse path, letter-lands' median section error is 0.05 seconds against Study 15's 0.08, and peaceful-dreams holds at 0.11. The predictions went four for four, and the second is the satisfying one: eat-all-the-clocks, exploratory in every prior study because its chart was wrong, drops from a 1.99 second median error to 0.09 with the band's corrected chart and is now gate-grade on every measure, confirming Study 12's verdict that the chart, not the aligner, was the bottleneck, this time by the fix rather than the failure. The verdict delivered: adoption validated, ship with confidence. Two asks stand: the LAST-SOUND ring-out refinement from Study 15, still visible in peaceful-dreams' tail sections, and the medianLocal clause in production's samePiece, promoted from recommendation to urgent ask. The urgent ask has since shipped: Stem Shovel AND-ed the local-cost clause into its production samePiece two days later, citing this study's escapee pair by name in the commit message, and Study 16b validated the shipped code against this study's full pairing matrix with a perfect sheet.

body.heading: The Question Study 13 Left
body.html: Study 13's closing guidance was explicit: if the chord feature matters, the next investment is Basic Pitch's successor on real timbres, not more model. Study 17 measured three zero-model successors, all built from things production already holds: per-stem transcription (the app stores the stems separately, and Study 13's path summed them first, feeding Basic Pitch the polyphonic mixture it fails on), bar-pooled chroma into production's own template matcher (nothing requires its 12-bin profile to come from transcribed notes), and ChordMini, the neural reader that lost Study 10's synthetic chord gate and had never been scored on real audio with bar-aligned chord truth, because that truth did not exist until Study 12. A conditional reconciler arm rode on the winner. The anchor gate passed exactly: the current path reproduced Study 13 arm 1 to the digit, 29 of 76 gated and 24 of 86 exploratory, before any new number was read.

body.heading: The Rematch
body.html: ChordMini on the mix, its native domain, reads the gated recording at 59 of 76 bars, 77.6 percent, and the exploratory song at 53 of 86. That passes the successor gate at 37 with twenty-two bars to spare and, more consequentially, passes 44 of 76, production's reconciled number from Study 14: a zero-model front end now beats code plus model, which flips the ship order. Study 10's synthetic verdict reversed on real audio, the home-field lesson's third instrument class after sections (LinkSeg) and the same-piece constant, and the rule is now three for three: no detector decision for real recordings gets made on synthetic numbers. A disclosed secondary read on the summed harmonic audio beat the mix on the gated song and collapsed on the exploratory one, so the registered choice of the mix survives its own alternative.

body.heading: Roots, Not Dressings
body.html: The gated chart's truth is 74 power-chord and 50 sus4 slots in 76 bars: this band writes roots and colors, not sevenths. ChordMini's gated credit came entirely through the registered power-chord allowance, with zero strict-first matches, because its vocabulary is root-level triads; it will never spell F#5 or Esus4, so the draft layer decides the dressing. A disclosed root-only read makes the real ranking visible: the current path holds 53 of 76 roots, per-stem 65, chroma 68, ChordMini 70, and 75 of 84 on the exploratory song. Every successor out-reads the anchor at the root level; the registered differences are quality dressing. The sharpest case is the chroma arm: 0 of 76 under the registered grade while holding 68 of 76 roots, because its pooled mass dresses nearly every right root in a hallucinated seventh, the exact over-read class its pre-registration self-proof surfaced and the brief disclosed, and the allowance admits only major, minor and power qualities. A quality fix needs a tuned mass threshold, which the arm was registered not to have, so it belongs to a registered follow-up or nowhere. Per-stem transcription split by stem inventory, and the mechanism is legible: letter-lands has no vocal stem and improved to 32; eat-all-the-clocks includes one, whose transcribed melody pollutes the merged harmony, and fell to 15 of 86. One song each way is a hypothesis, not a finding, but it ships with a rule attached: if per-stem transcription goes anywhere, vocal-labeled stems stay out of the chord evidence.

body.heading: The Reconciler's First Breaks
body.html: Arm E stacked Study 14's measured production reconciler path on the winner, with the registered design choice disclosed in the brief: ChordMini produces no note events, so the model saw ChordMini's chords beside the current path's transcribed note lines. The result is the study's most instructive number: 59 fell to 47, four fixes against sixteen breaks, the first breaks in three studies of reconciler runs, and the double-fix gate registered against Study 9's agreement trap failed for the first time, exactly as built. The mechanism is clean: ChordMini's chords are better than the transcribed notes support, so a pass that corrects the chords toward the notes destroys information. On the exploratory song it changed nothing. The reconciler's measured value is conditional on its evidence channel being the one that produced the draft, and the verdict delivered to the app says so: keep it on the Basic Pitch path it was measured on, and never run it on a non-note front end.

body.heading: Ship Guidance, and the Scorecard
body.html: Delivered to Stem Shovel in order of weight: ChordMini on the mix is the measured chord front end for real recordings, about 30 MB of hash-pinned ONNX weights already vendored since Study 10, four to six seconds a song on CPU, zero API spend, lifting the real number from 38 to 78 percent registered and from 53 to 70 of 76 at the root level; its root-level vocabulary ships with it, so the chart-draft layer renders the dressing, and for this catalog root-plus-power spelling covers most of the page; and the reconciler stays off its output. The scorecard kept the program honest: two predictions right, one half, three wrong, with the chroma favorite scoring zero under the registered grade and the reconciler prediction wrong in the instructive direction, two or fewer breaks predicted against sixteen measured. About $0.30 of the $2 fence, all of it in the two reconciler calls; arms A through D cost nothing.

body.heading: The Handoff, and the Registration
body.html: Stem Shovel ran the app's own chordsPerBar over the bench's stored Study 1 notes, reproduced the committed 424 of 440 exactly, and found two faults: a bass pickup into the next section renamed the bar it ended (the lowest note earned the root bonus whatever its length), and a power chord's ninth harmonic leaked a faint second over the old 5 percent presence line, so sus2 explained the bar by exactly the leak. v0.231.0 shipped the fixes: a bass note must sound for 15 percent of the bar, and a template tone under 12 percent of the profile counts as missing at a 0.12 cost. The synthetic verdict was clean, 424 to 439 of 440 with the power-chord song going 20 to 28 of 28. The open question was real audio: the app could only approximate it by rebuilding notes from Study 13's stored text lines, losing short notes and all start times, and that reconstruction read the presence rule as a wash or a small loss there. Its brief, committed verbatim in the bench repo, left the proper measurement to the bench and proposed the decision rule itself. The bench registered one parameterized port of the v0.231 matcher, pinned bar for bar against the retired port across all 440 fixture bars at the old constants, and measured the two rules separately, because a joint number would hide one rule behind the other.

body.heading: Four Gates, Four Passes
body.html: The anchor reproduced Study 13 arm 1 exactly for the third time, 29 of 76 and 24 of 86 on freshly re-transcribed notes, so every comparison sits on the stored footing rather than the approximation. The fixture table reproduced the handoff's five configurations to the digit through the bench's registered port, and the fixture gained matcher3 fields beside the v0.141 and v0.142 ones, nothing rewritten. On real audio the bass rule alone lifts the gated song from 29 to 39 of 76 and the exploratory song from 24 to 26 of 86, inside the registered central estimates. And the shipped pair reads 41 of 76 and 30 of 86, a net of plus six over bass-only across both songs, so the presence rule passes the author's own registered decision rule, keep it if and only if its real net is at least zero.

body.heading: The Overturned Hedge
body.html: The satisfying result is whose prediction failed. The handoff hedged its own presence rule, reading it from reconstructed notes as trading strict power-chord wins for majors with a weak third, and the bench registered that hedge as its prediction: a small negative net and a revert recommendation. The proper measurement overturned both. Strict-first accuracy rises too, 20 to 24 on the gated song and 18 to 23 on the exploratory one, so the gain is genuine readings rather than allowance credit. The lossy reconstruction was the artifact, not the rule, and the app's stated judgment, that an under-claimed power chord is the better failure for a chart hint, turned out right on the numbers as well as the merits. The disclosed sweep says the shipped constants sit on a plateau: a bass line of 0.10 readmits the pickups, 0.25 regresses the faster-bass exploratory song exactly as the handoff reasoned, and nothing in the grid earns a re-tune.

body.heading: The Floor Moves, the Ceiling Does Not
body.html: Two constants and one duration check take the real chord path from 38.2 to 53.9 percent on the gated song, which is exactly Study 13's reconciled 41 of 76: the free code change is worth as much on this song as the language-model reconciler pass. The ordering from Study 17 is unchanged and the report says so plainly: ChordMini on the mix still reads 59 of 76, eighteen bars past the improved matcher, so the front-end swap remains the measured next step. v0.231.0 raises the floor the app already ships. The hint baseline for anything measured after it moves from 29 to 41 of 76, and future studies gate their anchors against the version they pin. The verdict delivered: ship stands, nothing to change.

body.heading: The Port, and What Gating It Means
body.html: Study 17's verdict was that the neural chord reader on the original mix beats everything the note path can reach on real audio. The app acted on it: version 0.236.0 reads a song's chords from its mix on the server, with the whole Study 17 pipeline rebuilt in TypeScript. The pieces that could drift are exactly the pieces that were rewritten: librosa's constant-Q transform became a baked plan of sparse kernels over a short-time Fourier transform, with a 255-tap Kaiser half-band filter standing in for the reference resampler; the network runs under a WebAssembly ONNX runtime instead of Python's; the smoothing and the per-bar vote were retyped. The app's brief asked the bench to gate the port so the bench's numbers remain the app's, and proposed the pass lines itself: frame agreement of at least 99.5 percent, and per-bar scores within one bar of Study 17. The brief promised a parity table from the app's own run and the committed file did not contain it, so every number in this study was measured fresh. The bench ran the app's code as committed, imported from a worktree pinned at the shipping commit, against the Python reference exactly as Study 10 pinned it, on the bench's own decoded audio, so the gates isolate the rewritten pieces.

body.heading: Perfect Parity
body.html: Zero disagreeing frames. On all four public Badverbs mixes, 7,102 frames in total, the TypeScript pipeline's per-frame label equals the Python reference's, and the frame counts match exactly per song. The transform, the resampler, the inference and the smoothing reproduce numpy and librosa at the level that matters, the argmax. The registered prediction said at least 99.9 percent with any differences at window edges or label boundaries; the measurement left nothing to locate. On the two songs with chord truth, the app's per-bar vote reads 59 of 76 on the gated song and 53 of 86 on the exploratory one, Study 17's registered numbers to the bar rather than merely within the one-bar tolerance. The pre-registration checks had already pinned the label maps: the app's chart-symbol file is the bench's vocabulary map, 170 entries with zero differences, and the vocabulary order matches index for index.

body.heading: The Two Bars of Daylight
body.html: The study's one finding beyond the passes came from an internal cross-check: the app's vote run over the reference's own frames, compared with the reference's own per-bar answer. They differ at exactly two bars of one song, and both bars are the same case, an exact five-to-five frame tie between F sharp major and F sharp minor. Numpy's argmax breaks a tie toward the lower vocabulary index and says F sharp minor; the app's vote breaks it toward the first label the bar encounters and says F sharp major. The truth at both bars is the power chord F sharp five, the grading allowance admits either reading, and the score is identical either way. Tie-break order on exact ties is the entire remaining daylight between the two implementations, and it is disclosed here rather than papered over.

body.heading: What Stands
body.html: Ship stands, nothing to change. The standing rule from Study 17 rides along in the shipped code's own comments: the app never runs the AI reconciler on the model's chords, because the one measured attempt broke sixteen right bars. The chord numbers the dashboard cites for real audio, 77.6 percent on the gated song, now describe the production feature itself, not a Python harness that resembles it. Zero model calls, zero dollars, about thirty seconds of compute per song.

studies.title: The color experiment: the notes cannot dress the model's chords, and the one surviving rule fails its held-out test by splitting 81 to zero
studies.eyebrow: Studies 20 and 20b · the refutation and its held-out sequel · 941 zero-spend cells
studies.indexLine: The chord reader has the roots; the band's charts are made of colors it never writes, 74 power-chord and 50 sus4 slots on the gated song alone. Stem Shovel proposed dressing the model's roots from the free note channel, and Study 20 refuted the whole candidate: 438 of 440 on the synthetic fixture collapsed to 22 of 76 on the real recording, the recoloring destroyed twenty bars of credit the bare model already had, and the negative control beat the candidate outright. One asset survived the wreck, a power-chord call that was right 22 of 23 times it fired. Study 20b froze that rule and took it to two songs whose charts the bench had never seen, registered before the truth arrived. It failed there too, and the way it failed is the finding: 81 percent on the power-chord song, zero percent on the sparse triadic one, sixteen fires and sixteen misses. The hint's precision is not a number, it is a function of arrangement density, and the rule cannot tell which song it is in. These are the program's first full refutations, published as found, including two registration errors the bench made and owns.

body.heading: The Candidate, and the Refutation
body.html: ChordMini has the roots, 70 of 76 and 75 of 84 bars, but it never writes what this band's charts are made of: power chords, sus colors, the occasional slash bass. The app proposed colorChord, a pure function that would dress the model's per-bar root in whatever color the bar's transcribed notes support, never touching the root. The bench verified every premise in the brief, registered pass lines at the shape the app suggested, built the candidate to spec with instruments pinned to the Study 18 matcher arithmetic, and added a strict grade through barmark, the band's own notation package, where F sharp five and F sharp are different answers. All four gates failed. The candidate read 438 of 440 on the synthetic fixture and 22 of 76 on the real recording, the sharpest home-field collapse the program has measured. Worse than useless, it was destructive: on the exploratory song the recoloring turned twenty allowance-credited bars into wrong sus and slash dressings, dropping root-level credit from 53 to 33. And the negative control, the shipped matcher's own templates with the root forced and sevenths allowed, beat the hand-built rules 48 to 36 strict, refuting the premise that fencing out sevenths was the protective piece.

body.heading: Why the Notes Cannot Color These Bars
body.html: The anatomy found the cause in the transcription, not the rules. On roughly fifty of the gated song's 74 power-chord bars, the re-transcribed note profile shows a third or a fourth above the 12 percent presence line that the recording's guitars never played: harmonic smear and bleed, the same artifact class Study 13 documented at the chromagram floor. On those bars the right color is unreachable by any profile-threshold rule, because the note evidence itself contradicts it. The sus rules were the damage, 33 calls across both songs and zero right. The slash rule was flagged before the run as unvalidatable, since no corpus anywhere holds a slash chord in truth, and behaved exactly that way: fourteen firings, all cost. The major-minor flip fired three times on a song whose truth contains no major or minor triad, and the registered decision rule dropped it. One cell in the wreckage pointed the other way: when the candidate said power chord, it was right 22 of 23 times on the gated song.

body.heading: The Held-Out Sequel
body.html: That 22 of 23 was observed after the fact, on data the bench had already seen, so it proved nothing by itself. Study 20b froze the rule exactly as measured and registered blind gates before the bench had looked at the held-out truth: Kevin confirmed every public Badverbs song carries a bar-level chart, the registration committed first, and the charts for peaceful-dreams and mop-heart arrived afterward, committed verbatim with their provenance recorded. A blind variant rode along as a disclosed secondary arm, the same rule with its absence tests computed above a fixed pitch floor, reasoned from the smear's register before any new data existed. The result: 60.9 percent held-out precision against the registered 75 percent line, and the split is the finding. On peaceful-dreams, a power-chord song, the rule read 81 percent, and on bars whose truth is a bare power chord it was perfect, 39 of 39; six more fires were power-class right but spelled X5 where the chart writes X5(7), a vocabulary gap, not a hearing error. On mop-heart, a sparse waltz-time song of plain major triads, it fired sixteen times and missed sixteen times: about five and a half transcribed notes a bar never put the third on the page, and the rule read that silence as a power chord. An absent third is evidence only when the arrangement is dense enough that a played third would have been transcribed. The blind variant was worse, 48.8 percent, because that song carries its thirds in the bass register the floor strips.

body.heading: The Bench's Own Errors, Disclosed
body.html: Two mistakes in these studies belong to the bench and are published beside the results. Registering Study 20, the bench reordered the brief's color rules so sus4 is tested before the power chord, because the literal order made sus4 unreachable; on real audio that interpretation cost three and eleven strict bars against the alternative, and the report carries both readings, with every gate failing either way. Registering Study 20b, the bench derived the anchor-reproduction constants from the wrong column, counting bare power-chord symbols where the frozen rule counts firings, which include power calls the full candidate had dressed with a slash. The gate failed as registered and was not re-thresholded; the diagnosis reproduces the firing record bar for bar from Study 20's committed results, so the pipeline itself was bit-exact, and the error was in the registration's arithmetic, not the instrument.

body.heading: What Stands
body.html: Nothing ships. The card's hedge stays exactly what Study 17 set: the chord reader will never spell a power chord or a sus voicing, and the app says so rather than guessing. The verdicts, delivered the same day each study closed, recommend no further spend unprompted; if the app ever wants a third pass, the data names its two ingredients, a density precondition and the chart's X5(7) spelling, registered fresh and blind. The program also banked a durable asset: bar-level truth for two more real songs, including a trap song of plain triads in waltz time that every future chord study should keep in its corpus. A benchmark that only publishes wins is an advertisement; these two entries are the receipts that this one is not.

body.heading: The Design, and One Pre-Data Decision
body.html: The two held-out charts arrived for Study 20b, after the reader shipped and after Study 19 gated its port, so for the model they are held out in the sense that matters: nothing in the pipeline or its studies ever touched them. The study ran the pinned reference pipeline on each song's mix over the aligned bar grid, exactly as every prior real-audio study, at zero spend. One grading decision had to be made before the data existed, and was registered: peaceful-dreams' chart writes X5(7) on 32 bars, and Study 13's power allowance keys on the quality 5 exactly. A power chord with an optional seventh declares no third either, so the registered primary grade extends the allowance to 5(7), changing nothing else, with a pin test proving it identical to the Study 13 grade wherever that quality is absent, both anchors, mop-heart, and the whole synthetic fixture, so no prior number could move.

body.heading: The Gates
body.html: S21-G1 passed exactly: letter-lands and eat-all-the-clocks reproduced 59 of 76 and 53 of 86 to the digit, the fourth reproduction of the anchor numbers. S21-G2 asked each held-out song for at least half of its chord-bearing bars under the extended allowance. mop-heart passed easily at 76.4 percent. peaceful-dreams missed by four bars, 73 of 153, and the gate fails as registered. The anatomy below is reported beside the gate, not in place of it.

body.heading: The Anatomy: Dialect, Not Hearing
body.html: peaceful-dreams' roots are 149 of 153, 97.4 percent, the best root performance the program has measured. The lost credit sits on the 62 bars, forty percent of the song, whose truth qualities the allowance vocabulary does not speak. On the 32 X5(7) bars the model answers X7 on 24, it hears the optional seventh, but 7 is not in the registered allowance set, so only its six plain-major answers credited. On the 30 D7sus4 bars it answers D7 or Dsus4, roots right on 29 of 30, each answer half of the truth, credit zero. The expected windfall from the 5(7) extension never came, six bars instead of the predicted fifteen to thirty, and for the best possible reason: the model was saying something more specific than the allowance anticipated. mop-heart is the opposite pole: plain major triads are the model's native vocabulary, and it read 107 of 140 bars exactly right, no allowance involved, with roots at 115 of 140, on the same sparse three-four arrangement whose silence the note-channel power hint misread sixteen times out of sixteen. A reader that hears the mix does not need the transcription to have written the third.

body.heading: What Stands
body.html: Nothing changes in the app; the reader is already shipped and Study 17's hedge already covers the colors. What changed is the evidence: the reader's roots now stand on four songs instead of two, 82 to 97 percent per song and 90.3 percent combined, and the colors it misses are half-heard rather than unheard, exactly the raw material a draft layer reads. That is the registered baseline for the recording-to-chart question. One lesson is registered for the program itself: allowance vocabularies are registered against each chart's own symbol census before the run, never patched after. Predictions: three right, including mop-heart's strict-equals-right landing exactly at 107, and two wrong, one of them wrong in the most informative direction.

studies.title: The bar grid from the recording alone: the sanity gate caught the bench, the decision gate failed everywhere, and the real limit is the ruler
studies.eyebrow: Study 22 · instrumentation · 910 zero-spend cells
studies.indexLine: An auto-written chart has no chart to align, so the recording-to-chart question stands on a prior one: can a usable bar grid come from the recording alone? The study's first run failed its own sanity gate at zero percent on every synthetic render and thereby proved the bench's registered metric defective: a blind downbeat estimate exists only modulo the bar period, and the index-paired scoring compared a 68-millisecond-accurate comb one bar shifted. The metric was replaced under the program's defective-grader rule and the re-run passed the sanity gate at 100 percent on all four renders. Then the decision gate failed in the deepest way available: even the least-squares ceiling, the best uniform grid fit to the truth itself, hits only 27 to 38 percent of truth bar starts within fifteen percent of a bar. The chart-anchored DTW truth that every chord study grades on resolves bar positions to a few hundred milliseconds, which per-bar chord grading happily tolerates and a bar-position gate cannot see through. The registered decision: the end-to-end study runs grid-given, and the no-chart grid stays open until the program owns finer truth than its own ruler.

table.summary: Both runs' gates, the amendment, the ceiling anatomy, and the detector's ladder behavior

body.heading: The Sanity Gate Did Its Job, On the Bench
body.html: The study registered three arms (a least-squares ceiling, a declared-tempo arm with a blind downbeat phase, and a fully blind detector arm) plus a sanity gate: the pipeline on each chart's synthetic reference render, whose true bar starts are exact, must hit at least 95 percent. The first run scored zero on all four renders. The cause was the bench's own registered metric: it paired grid index to bar index, but a blind phase estimate exists only modulo the period, so a comb that had landed 68 milliseconds from the render's downbeats scored nothing, one bar shifted. Per the program's rules the metric was replaced (lattice distance, each truth bar start against the nearest lattice point, with each arm's period reported beside its rate so a half-period lattice cannot take silent octave credit), the defective run's numbers disclosed as seen, and the re-run passed at 100.0 percent on all four renders.

body.heading: The Decision Gate, and the Ruler
body.html: On the real recordings the declared-tempo arm read 8.5 to 68.8 percent against the registered 80 percent line, and the ceiling arm read 27.3 to 37.9 percent. When the best uniform grid that can be fit to the truth itself misses two-thirds of that truth at fifteen percent of a bar, with around 400 milliseconds of mean error against tolerances of 122 to 280, no derivable grid could have passed and none did. The mechanism is the program's own instrumentation: the chart-anchored DTW truth is quantized at 93 milliseconds and its path wanders, so consecutive truth bar durations swing by hundreds of milliseconds. Per-bar chord grading tolerates that, which is why Study 21 read 97 percent roots on these exact grids, but a bar-position gate is finer than the ruler, and whether the bands also genuinely drift cannot be separated from the ruler's wander. One blind-arm result stands cleanly: the shipped detector's tempo landed on a Study 11 ladder rung of the declared tempo on all four songs, and the raw-octave grids score under 30 percent, so the ladder fold is load-bearing for any future grid work.

body.heading: What Stands
body.html: The registered decision: the end-to-end draft study runs grid-given, taking its bars from the chart-anchored alignment like every chord study before it, and the no-chart grid is recorded as open, unmeasurable until the program owns truth finer than a few hundred milliseconds per bar. Human-tapped downbeats on one or two songs would unlock it. Predictions: two right, two wrong (one decisively, the ceiling), one not evaluable, and the first prediction wrong as registered then right after the amendment its failure forced.

body.heading: The Composition

body.heading: The Gates: Four Failures on the Chart Channel
body.html: Peaceful-dreams' chart does not parse at all. Eat-all-the-clocks renders 68 of its 86 bars and mop-heart 84 of 140, so the structure gate passes only on letter-lands, and with bars missing the index-paired root grades collapse. Zero of peaceful-dreams' 62 dialect bars survive on the chart channel. The failure modes are specific and legible: the model writes cell-level repeats, a bar reading D5 x8, which the band's notation does not define and the parser refuses, and it under-writes section repeats. The production prompt's own compact example, D(7)sus4 followed by D5 x2, invited exactly this generalization.

body.heading: The JSON Channel: the Music Was Right
body.html: The same four answers' chords fields are bar-exact on every song and grade as the strongest chord numbers the program has produced. Letter-lands reads 72 of 76 roots, above its hint's 70. Peaceful-dreams reads 151 of 153 roots, above the reader's own 149, with strict credit on 84 bars against the reader's 20, and eleven of the 62 dialect bars exactly right: D7sus4, which appears in the prompt's notation examples, written strictly eleven times where the reader alone scores zero by vocabulary, and G7 on ten G5(7) bars, the seventh heard and the chart's spelling absent from every example, the same half-heard signature Study 21 measured in the reader. Mop-heart reads 131 of 140 roots and 129 strict. The one true regression is eat-all-the-clocks, whose roots drop from the hint's 74 to 68 of 84 on the vocal-heavy song. Had the gates sat on this channel, three of four would have passed; they were registered on the chart channel because the chart is what ships, and they are not re-thresholded.

body.heading: What Stands

The draft already returns bar-exact chords and section starts as data; a chart built from those fields by code would have passed the validity, structure and color gates on this pilot, leaving only eat-all-the-clocks' root regression to examine. The verdict to the app names that as the recommended design, with constraining the prompt's chart examples to row notation as the weaker second option, and notes that one example line showing the G5(7) spelling would likely convert the ten G7 bars. Any re-test is a new registration. The prediction scorecard is a clean sweep of the right kind: all five predictions wrong on the gated channel, and every predicted mechanism, parse quality, hint-following roots, 7sus4-led dialect recovery, visible in the JSON. The bench predicted the music and failed to predict the serialization.

body.heading: The Arms
body.html: Both arms build the grid a chartless song would actually have: the period from the song's declared bpm and meter, the bar count from the recording's length, the transcription binned by that grid, the shipped reader's labels over that grid as hints, and Study 23's prompt, model and call shape verbatim. B2 anchors the grid at the aligned truth's first bar start, simulating a user who taps the downbeat perfectly once. B1 takes Study 22's blind onset-comb phase, the zero-UX option. Gates sat on the JSON chords channel, index-paired against the chart, with the grid-given baselines recomputed in-run from Study 23's committed results.

body.heading: Gate One: the Perfect Tap Fails Everywhere
body.html: The tap arm was the worst arm measured. Roots against the grid-given baseline: letter-lands 39 of 76 against 72, eat-all-the-clocks 21 of 84 against 68, peaceful-dreams 64 of 153 against 151, mop-heart 53 of 140 against 131. The mechanical anatomy leaves no room for argument: B2's grid hits the truth lattice at exactly one bar per song, its own anchor, and its mean per-bar error runs 3.3 to 8.4 seconds, multiple bars adrift by mid-song. The phase was perfect by construction, so the entire error is the period. The declared bpm is not the recording's tempo, and a uniform grid built from it walks off the music within a dozen bars no matter where it starts.

body.heading: The Inversion: the Blind Comb Beats the Tap
body.html: Gate two passed, but inverted: the blind comb landed above the perfect tap on all four songs (52, 51, 138 and 133 roots), with mop-heart at 133 of 140, above its own grid-given baseline. Two mechanisms, both visible in the committed records, neither a vindication of blind grids. The comb fits the whole recording's onsets, so its wrong-by-whole-bars phase acts as a crude mid-song recentering of the wrong-period lattice, roughly halving the mean error. And these songs' progressions repeat, so index-paired roots forgive a grid shifted by whole loops. B1's grids are still not truth, seven lattice hits at best; the scores survive because the music is periodic, not because the bars are right. The dialect casualty confirms the stakes: peaceful-dreams' 62 chart-dialect bars, eleven exactly right grid-given, drop to four under the tap and six under the comb.

body.heading: The Shootout and the Decision
body.html: The $0 side-measurement answered the tap-free downbeat question: graded by circular anchor error against the truth's first bar start, the onset comb hits three of four songs within 15 percent of a bar, the chord-change comb two, the bass comb one, and the music-start anchor two by circular error. A correction, dated the same day and found by Study 24's variant data: this entry first said the music-start anchor caught letter-lands' 7.15 second intro at 121 ms, and it did not. Its anchor there is t equals zero, the recording opens with a loud note four bars before the charted music, and the 121 ms figure is mod-period coincidence, exactly what a comb would report; across the corpus the first-loud-note anchor finds the audio start, not the charted start, so nothing measured yet detects an uncharted intro. So anchoring within the bar is nearly solved and it is the wrong question: B2 just proved a perfect anchor is worth nothing under a wrong period. The registered decision table fires its third row: uniform grids are insufficient even anchored, and the feature needs alignment-grade grids or the true tempo measured from the recording. The cheapest candidate reuses the shipped reader with zero new UX, extending the chord-change comb from a phase search to a joint phase-and-period search, and is registered as the program's next study. The prediction scorecard is honest about the surprise: the gate-one failure was called but not its universality, and the comb-beats-tap inversion was predicted in the opposite direction.
